title: Dynamic Relational Transitioning Geometry (TRPG): code, data and documents
description: A relational, entanglement-based framework that reproduces known physics and predicts normal-ordered neutrino masses of 0.36, 8.6 to 8.7 and 50.1 to 50.3 meV (sum 0.0591 to 0.0594 eV), and a strong coupling of 0.1178 at the Z, awaiting measurement. This release contains every calculation script (all run with one command), the every-particle-to-every-particle workbook, the paper (version 1.4.1) and the later test scripts. Version 1.4.1 states more fully how AI assistants were used (paper Acknowledgements); no result changed. Version 1.4.0 restates the framework as five rules and one bet (one matrix of relationships read in three roles, balance of pull and resistance, the 45-degree rule for leptons, nothing extra, and a smooth start); keeps a short start phase driven by the stiffness of space as the alternative start (it predicts r = 0.0040 and a ripple tilt of 0.963, disfavoured by CMB plus DESI, which the main line follows); adds the exact right-angled quark triangle (lambda = 1/sqrt(20), A = sqrt(2/3), beta = 22.5 deg, gamma = 67.5 deg) as a dated lead; shows that no discrete charge rule gives the far-side weight without an anomaly; records eleven further tests that failed, each with its script; and gives where each open problem stands after independent rechecks. No particle-physics number changed. Version 1.3.3 recalibrates every headline number to the Particle Data Group's 2026 values and JUNO 2026, and lists every test that was set after an earlier attempt failed. Version 1.3.2 was revised after three rounds of outside review: full 3x3 seesaw, compact stars as self-bound strange stars with the Bodmer-Witten check, the force strengths stated as a crossing with a boundary condition, and the neutrino mixing prediction checked against JUNO 2026 (2.3 sigma high). Website: https://trpgphysics.org
